s: Return to me, and I will return to you. Visions of horsemen among the myrtles, four horns and four craftsmen.
A man measures Jerusalem, which will have no walls, for God will be a wall of fire around it.
The high priest Joshua is given clean garments. God will bring his servant the Branch.
The golden lampstand and two olive trees: not by might, nor by power, but by my Spirit.
A flying scroll and a woman in a basket carried away.
Four chariots go out. Joshua is crowned as a sign of the Branch who will build the temple.
God wants justice and mercy rather than empty fasting.
God will return to Zion and Jerusalem will be the city of truth.
Rejoice, daughter of Zion: your king comes to you, humble and riding on a donkey.
God will care for his flock and bring his people home.
The good shepherd is paid thirty pieces of silver.
They shall look on him whom they have pierced and mourn for him.
A fountain will be opened to cleanse from sin. Strike the shepherd and the sheep will scatter.
The day of the Lord: living waters will flow from Jerusalem, and the Lord will be king over all the earth.

9: Zion's king comes riding on a donkey. Jesus fulfils this on Palm Sunday.
In older English “corn” meant any grain, such as wheat or barley.
